summary: The English of the four sayings is sound and follows Bartenura and Rambam; one real fault is in 2:16, where 'know the granting of the reward ... in the world to come' loses the nominal clause (the reward is given in the time to come). The main faults are lexical: many tokens point to BDB proper names (Baal, Bajith, Sacar, Mattan, Baruch, Raham, Ezem) or to wrong entries (the noun 'length' for the adjective אֶרֶךְ, 'father' for לָבֹא, 'another' for חוֹרִין), and are moved to the Jastrow entries the pack lists or have their sense removed. The 2:13 apparatus and grammar wrongly said Joel 2:13 reads אֵל (it is Jonah 4:2 and Vilna that read it), the 2:14 apparatus gave Rambam's proof text as Job/Psalms instead of Jer 1:12, and Bartenura's שְׂכָרְךָ 'He hired you' was misread as 'your reward'. The morphology is mostly right; patches correct the article in בַּ and לֶ, the participle וְנִחָם, אָרֵךְ, בָּרַךְ, רַחֲמִים, חוֹר, the adverb הַרְבֵּה and a suffix form.

patches.value: Rabbi Shimon says: Be careful in reciting the Shema and in the Prayer. And when you pray, do not make your prayer a fixed routine, but a plea for mercy and supplication before the Omnipresent, blessed be He, as it is said (Joel 2): “For He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in kindness, and relenting of the evil.” And do not be wicked in your own eyes.
patches.reason: וּבַתְּפִלָּה has the article (בַּ): 'the Prayer', the statutory Tefillah, set beside the Shema and timed like it (Bartenura: each prayer at its time). The reference (יואל ב) is the edition's parenthesis, not the mishnah's words: keep it in parentheses rather than as 'in Joel 2'.

patches.value: nifal participle (the qamets under ח marks the participle; the perfect is נִחַם): 'relenting', 'changing one's mind' about the harm, the last of a series of attributes. The cited sense is Jastrow's Hithpael 'to be sorry, reconsider': the entry gives no Nifal.

patches.value: עֶצֶם 'bone', hence 'substance, self'; with the suffix, 'yourself'. Jastrow sense 3 cites this mishnah: 'be not a wicked man in thine own sight'.

value: הֱוֵי and תְּהִי are both forms of הָיָה: the contracted imperative 'be!' and the jussive-type imperfect after אַל, 'do not be'.
אַל תַּעַשׂ is a prohibition: אַל with the imperfect. אֶלָּא 'but' sets the right prayer against the wrong one, with the verb 'make' understood.
קֶבַע is the opposite of תַּחֲנוּנִים: a fixed act versus a plea; רַחֲמִים וְתַחֲנוּנִים are the two things the prayer should be.

The mishnah quotes Joel 2:13 as it stands there: כִּי חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם הוּא, without אֵל (the Vilna text adds אֵל, as in Jonah 4:2). אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם is a construct chain: אֶרֶךְ is the construct of the adjective אָרֵךְ 'long', 'long of nostrils (anger)', meaning patient.
חַנּוּן, רַחוּם, אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם, רַב חֶסֶד and the nifal participle וְנִחָם are a series of attributes of God, all predicates of הוּא.
בִּפְנֵי עַצְמְךָ, literally 'in the face of your self', is an idiom whose sense is disputed; see the note.
patches.reason: the old note implied that Joel 2:13 reads אֵל; it does not (Joel: כִּי חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם הוּא; Jonah 4:2: כִּי אַתָּה אֵל חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם). It also took אֶרֶךְ as a noun.

value: Joel 2:13: כִּי חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם הוּא אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב חֶסֶד וְנִחָם עַל הָרָעָה. The base text quotes Joel exactly, without אֵל. Bartenura's lemma (כִּי אֵל חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם הוּא) and the Vilna text read אֵל, as in Jonah 4:2 (כִּי אַתָּה אֵל חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם); Rabbeinu Yonah cites the verse in Jonah's wording, and his copyist notes that by our mishnah's reading the verse is Joel 2:13.
Vilna reads בקרית for בִּקְרִיאַת (2:13.6); Vilna adds אל in the quotation (כי אל חנון ורחום הוא); Vilna's reference adds the verse number (יואל ב, יג).
patches.reason: Joel 2:13 has no אֵל: the old line said the reverse. The Vilna variants were misdescribed: Vilna adds the word אל and the verse number יג, not 'a variant of the chapter number'.
Rabbeinu Yonah's reading (do not be wicked in your own eyes, so as to despair of repentance) is the reading the English adopts, with Rambam; it is not merely recorded.

patches.value: Rabbi Elazar says: Be diligent in learning Torah, and know what to answer an Epicurean. And know before whom you toil. And faithful is the master of your work to pay you the reward of your labor.
patches.reason: a comma and a capital 'And' joined two sentences; the Hebrew has two.
the speaker is the Tanna R. Elazar son of Arakh (2:8); Jastrow sense 3 names him.
Jastrow 'several Tannaim: ... E. b. Arakh'.
the only sense of bdbs:תּוֹרָה in the data is 'custom, manner, law (of man)', wrong here; the pack lists Jastrow תּוֹרָה, 'the Law of Moses'.
Jastrow sense 1: teaching, law, esp. the Law of Moses.
מַה שֶּׁ is the relative 'what, whatever' (1.2), not the interrogative 'what?' (1.1).
לִפְנֵי is the prepositional use (1.7.1), not 'presence, person' (1.2).

Jastrow sense 5: (in compounds) owner of, master of.

patches.value: לָךְ is the mishnaic form of 'to you' (masculine); biblical Hebrew writes לְךָ, as at 2:16.
patches.reason: a learner meets לָךְ as a feminine form in the Bible.

value: The saying has no direct biblical quotation. Rambam's proof texts on the sense of שְׁקִידָה are Jer 1:12 (כִּי שֹׁקֵד אֲנִי עַל דְּבָרִי) and Prov 8:34 (לִשְׁקֹד עַל דַּלְתֹתַי יוֹם יוֹם).
Vilna reads ללמוד for לִלְמֹד (2:14.6) and פעולתך for פְּעֻלָּתֶךְ (2:14.24).
Rabbeinu Yonah's lemmas read מה שתשיב את אפקורוס (for לְאֶפִּיקוֹרוֹס) and ומי הוא בעל מלאכתך (for וְנֶאֱמָן הוּא בַעַל מְלַאכְתְּךָ): 'and who is the master of your work, who will pay you'.
patches.reason: Rambam's first proof text is Jer 1:12, not 'Job 8 / Ps 69'. Rabbeinu Yonah's lemma has a different reading of the last clause, which was not recorded.

patches.value: Rambam: you must learn what to answer the Epicureans among the idolaters and refute them; with an Israelite Epicurean one does not speak at all, for argument only makes him scorn more and he has no remedy. And though you learn the nations' opinions, guard that none of them rises in your heart, and know that He before whom you labor knows the secret of your heart.
patches.reason: the summary left out Rambam's limit: the answer is for the gentile Epicurean, not the Israelite one.
bdbs:שָׂכָר is the personal name Sacar; Jastrow שָׂכָר 'wages, reward' is in the pack.
Jastrow sense 1: wages, reward.
bdbs:בַּעַל is the name and the god Baal; Jastrow sense 5 'master of' is meant.
Jastrow sense 5: owner of, master of.
bdbs:בַּיִת is the place name Bajith; Jastrow בַּיִת sense 2 'house, household' is in the pack.
Jastrow sense 2: house, household, home.

patches.value: He used to say: It is not for you to finish the work, and you are not free to desist from it. If you have learned much Torah, they give you much reward. And faithful is the master of your work to pay you the reward of your labor. And know that the granting of the reward of the righteous is in the world to come.
patches.reason: the last clause is a nominal clause, the object of וְדַע, with לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא as its predicate: 'the giving of the reward of the righteous is in the time to come'. 'Know the granting ... in the world to come' loses the predication and is not English.

patches.value: He was saying: not upon-you the-work to-finish, and-not you son-of free-men to-be-idle from-it. If you-learned Torah much, giving to-you reward much. And-faithful he master-of your-work that-he-pays to-you reward-of your-labor. And-know giving-of their-reward of righteous for-the-future to-come.
patches.reason: חוֹרִין is plural, 'free men'; לֶעָתִיד has the article and ל, 'for the future'.

patches.value: לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא is translated 'in the world to come', since Bartenura and Rambam both say it means לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא; the literal sense is 'for the time that is to come'. נוֹתְנִים 'they give' is an impersonal plural: 'one gives you', that is, you are given. The last clause is a nominal clause, the object of וְדַע, with לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא as its predicate: 'that the giving of their reward, of the righteous, is in the time to come'; the English supplies 'that' and 'is'.
patches.reason: the old note said Rabbeinu Yonah takes 'they give you' of the master; his comment on that clause (2:16:3) says only that the one who learns more gains more. It also called the last clause ambiguous between 'that' and 'when', which the grammar does not support.
לֹא is an adverb whose entry lists a sense, as at 2:16.4.
בֶן is 'son of'; the gloss 'free' belongs to חוֹרִין.

patches.value: Bartenura: the Holy One, blessed be He, did not hire you (שְׂכָרְךָ) to finish all of it, so that you would lose your wages if you did not finish it. And lest you say 'I will not learn and will take no wages', it says 'you are not free to be idle': against your will the yoke is laid on you to work.
patches.reason: שְׂכָרְךָ here is the verb 'He hired you' (subject הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, then the infinitive לִגְמֹר), not 'your reward'.
בַּ (patach and dagesh in ת) contains the definite article: 'in the Prayer'.

morphemes.parse: qal, participle passive, masculine, singular, absolute

patches.reason: a qal passive participle is a verb form: pos verb, lemma the root's qal perfect בָּרַךְ. The lemma בָּרוּךְ leads to the personal name Baruch.
אֶרֶךְ in אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם is the construct of the adjective אָרֵךְ 'long', not the noun אֹרֶךְ 'length'.

verdicts.comment: 'Be careful in reciting the Shema and in the Prayer' carries his 'at its proper time' without narrowing it.
'a fixed routine' is his first sense (a debt to be discharged) and his second (a set reading, not supplication).
his lemma reads אֵל, with Jonah 4:2 and Vilna; the base text, which quotes Joel 2:13, does not. Recorded in the apparatus.
the English takes Rambam's reading, which Bartenura cites; his own two readings are recorded.
'do not be wicked in your own eyes' is his reading; 'fixed routine' is his burden to be got rid of.
'Epicurean' is kept with his sense of one who scorns the Torah.
'diligent' carries both his senses, eager and constant.
the English does not narrow 'Epicurean'; his limit to the gentile is now in the summary.
the English keeps the parable; the note gives his reading.
he reads the saying as a parable, and the English keeps it one.
the English agrees; the summary misread שְׂכָרְךָ and is patched.
'in the world to come' is his לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
'in the world to come' is his לעולם הבא.
